title: Thursday’s analyst upgrades and downgrades
text:
Inside the Market’s roundup of some of today’s key analyst actions
The upside to Bombardier Inc. ( BBD.B-T ) justifies the risk, according to Vertical Research analyst Robert Stallard, who thinks its stock has moved past a “double or nothing equity bet.”
Initiating coverage of the stock with a “buy” rating, Mr. Stallard sees potential for the Montreal-based company’s free cash flow to expand from its current break-even position to $2-billion by 2023, seeing improved prospects for both its C Series and business jets.
He set a target price of $5.70 for Bombardier shares. The average target is $5.96, according to Bloomberg data.
BMO Nesbitt Burns analyst Alexander Pearce raised his rating for Cameco Corp. ( CCO-T , CCJ-N ) in reaction to the Wednesday announcement that the Tax Court of Canada has ruled in its favour in its dispute of the reassessments issued by Canada Revenue Agency for the 2003, 2005 and 2006 tax years.
Moving its stock to “outperform” from “market perform,” Mr. Pearce said the decision sets a positive precedent, projecting it could be worth as much as $5 per share. He also thinks the decision could sway the decision for the remaining years under reassessment by the CRA to 2012 as well as subsequent years through to 2017.
“The decision likely removes a significant overhang from the stock and should reinstate its position as the premier investment for uranium exposure," he said.
Mr. Pearce raised his target for Cameco shares to $16 from $14. The average target is $15.13.
Invesque Inc. ( IVQ.U-T ) currently provides investors with a “compelling” entry point, according to Industrial Alliance Securities analyst Brad Sturges, leading him to raise his rating for the Indiana-based real estate investment trust to “strong buy” from “buy.”
“We are upgrading Invesque Inc. … to reflect the company’s attractive 9-per-cent yield and discount valuation that has recently widened due to relative underperformance, and management’s historical track record of strategic execution and creation of unitholder value,” he said. “We believe that Invesque may narrow its discount valuation in the next 12 months through: 1) greater investor awareness of its unique Canadian-listed investment opportunity; 2) improved EBITDAR coverage ratios, particularly for SNF operator tenants; and 3) further execution of its external acquisition growth strategy.”
Mr. Sturges made the move following a recent tour of Invesque’s Ottawa medical office buildings (MOB), which included assets recently required from Mohawk Medical Properties REIT. He said the tour showed the platform growth potential from the Mohawk relationship.
“Our two key takeaways consist of: 1) Invesque’s current MOB acquisition pipeline in the U.S. and Canada is estimated to be around $200-million, and the company has a strategic focus on consolidating the highly fragmented U.S. Class B, multi-tenant, off-campus MOB property sector that currently offers going-in unlevered yields of 7 per cent to 8 per cent, and 2) Invesque is generally targeting annual same-property rental income growth between 2 per cent and 3 per cent for its MOB platform,” said Mr. Sturges.
“We also recently hosted a number of institutional marketing meetings for Invesque in September. These three main takeaways from the meetings include: 1) Invesque remains very much under the radar for investors in our opinion; 2) the recent sell-off in Invesque’s shares may be related to a churn in its investor base including former unitholders of Mohawk that were not subject to a lock-up period; and 3) discussions mainly centred around recent portfolio transactions, future growth prospects, and the macro U.S. SNF environment.”
The analyst maintained a target price of US$9 per unit. The average is US$9.42.
Highlighting the potential for significant growth to its service business, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee initiated coverage of Apple Inc. ( AAPL-Q ) with an “overweight” rating.
“[Apple] is transforming from a hardware company to a services company faster than investors had expected, which is driving financial and valuation upside," he said.
“We expect increasing appreciation of acceleration in growth, along with greater visibility into earnings and cash flow with increasing mix of Services."
Expecting Apple to “comfortable achieve” its target of US$48-billion in service revenue by fiscal 2020, Mr. Chatterjee set a target price of US$272, which exceeds the average of US$233.44.
“While Apple's leadership position in the premium smartphone market is well understood by investors, we still see considerable upside to the stock from current levels," he said.
Calling its third-quarter results “solid” and seeing its CEO transition as a “positive,” Desjardins Securities analyst Gary Ho raised his near-term financial expectations for AGF Management Ltd. ( AGF.B-T )
“We foresee a few near- or medium-term positive catalysts: (1) improving fund performance leading to 60 per cent of AUM [assets under management] above median over three years; (2) net retail flows improving relative to industry; (3) investors recognizing a proper valuation for S&W [Smith & Williamson]; (4) restoring management’s credibility; and (5) all of these factors leading to better sentiment and valuation."
Mr. Ho moved his fiscal 2018 EBITDA and earnings per share expectations to $68.4-million and 88 cents, respectively, from $68.3-million and 77 cents.
He maintained a “buy” rating and $8.50 target for AGF shares. The average is $7.75.
“It remains our preferred name in the sector given its attractive valuation (3.2 times our estimated 2019 wealth management EBITDA; we value the S&W stake at a conservative $262-million), good cost containment, net sales turnaround (robust retail net inflows in September), management transition that we are positive on and the S&W jewel which potentially provides upside to our C$8.50 target price,” he said.
RBC Dominion Securities analyst Nathan Piper recommends investors initiate or add to their positions in Gran Tierra Energy Inc. ( GTE-T ) ahead of coming drilling catalysts.
“Gran Tierra is set to grow production around 15 per cent year-over-year to reach 50,000 barrels per day by 2020,” he said. “This is entirely cash flow funded and driven, largely, by ongoing development/appraisal drilling on the Acordionero field (GTE 100 per cent). The asset should deliver reserves increases as higher recovery factors are reflected (moving 41mmbbls 3P into 2P/1P) and the extent of the field is better defined. Despite recent share price strength the company still trades at a 20-per-cent discount core NAV (2P reserves) vs the sector average premium of 5 per cent. We anticipate this discount should unwind into year-end with the potential for drilling catalysts to accelerate the rerating.”
With a “top pick” rating (unchanged), Mr. Piper raised his target by a dime to $6.50. The average is $5.92.
“The stock is up around 40 per cent year-to-date but remains one of the least expensive in our coverage, trading at a 20-per-cent discount to core NAV (vs the sector average of a 5-per-cent premium),” the analyst said.
